passage:
Thursday. Rekha Ma'am brought a police officer to our class today. I hid behind Arjun because Dadi always says, "Behave or the police will take you away." My legs went funny.
But the officer said her job is to help. She said if you get lost, find someone in uniform, say your name and your parents' phone number, and stay put. She made us say ours three times. I asked, "Do you take naughty children?" She laughed and said, "No, I help find their mummies."
I am still a bit scared of the whistle. But I know my number now. I will say it loud and polite.
Sachin

qa.q: Who brought the police officer to class?
qa.a: Rekha Ma'am brought the police officer.

qa.q: What was Sachin feeling when hiding behind Arjun?
qa.a: Sachin was scared, because Dadi always says the police will take naughty children away, and Sachin's legs went funny.

qa.q: What will Sachin do if lost, after the officer's talk?
qa.a: Sachin will find someone in uniform, say the name and parents' phone number loudly and politely, and stay put.

qa.q: How might the officer have seen Sachin's question about naughty children?
qa.a: The officer laughed and answered kindly, so she probably understood that children can be frightened of the uniform and wanted to reassure Sachin.

grounding: A child who fears the police because adults said they take you away learns that police help, and to be cautious yet respectful.

passage:
At the temple fair, Anjali, eight, let go of her mother Bhavna's hand to watch a puppet show. When the crowd moved, she was alone among strangers' legs. Bhavna always said, "Behave, or the police will take you." Now Anjali saw a constable near the bus stand with a stiff cap and a whistle, and her knees shook.
Then she remembered the school talk: find someone in uniform, say your name and number. She walked up with folded hands. "Namaste. I am lost. I am Anjali. My mother is Bhavna. Papa's number is..."
The constable crouched and dialled. In a few minutes Bhavna came running. Later she said, "I should not have said that about the police."

qa.q: Who did Anjali find near the bus stand?
qa.a: Anjali found a constable near the bus stand.

qa.q: What was Anjali feeling as she saw the constable?
qa.a: Anjali felt frightened, with shaking knees, because her mother had always said the police would take her.

qa.q: What choice did Anjali make that got her back to her mother?
qa.a: She remembered the school talk and walked up to the constable, said her name and number politely, and the constable dialled.

qa.q: Why might Bhavna have said she should not have talked about the police that way?
qa.a: Bhavna saw that the fear she had put in Anjali nearly stopped Anjali from asking for help, and wanted to change it.

grounding: A child sees police as scary because adults said they take you away, and learns that police are there to help, staying cautious yet respectful.
